result.summary: This PR reworks the libbitcoinkernel C logging API so that logging options and log streams (Logger objects) are set per-connection and associated with Context objects, rather than being global. It removes the unsafe btck_logging_disable() function and eliminates the default behavior of buffering log messages in a 1MB buffer before any logger is attached. The change is deliberately not backwards compatible but is intended to make the API easier to reason about and forward-compatible with a later change (#30342) that would let different log streams receive different messages.
result.problem: The current kernel logging API is confusing and inefficient: multiple log streams can be created but all receive the same messages because options are set globally, streams are not referenced by the Context, unattached loggers silently accumulate messages in a 1MB buffer, and btck_logging_disable() can abort the program if misused. This affects every consumer of libbitcoinkernel's C API, especially language-binding authors who must map onto this interface.

open_concerns: stickies-v and stringintech prefer waiting for #30342 (per-connection logger instances) before locking in an API shape, arguing the interim API's signatures imply per-connection isolation that doesn't yet exist and could confuse users.

stickies-v raised lifetime/ownership questions about Context holding a raw BCLog::Logger* pointer when the logger could be destroyed first; author proposed a use_count safeguard but this has not been implemented in the current diff.
Six other open PRs touch overlapping kernel logging surface, and the discussion shows the underlying design direction (global vs per-connection logging state) is still contested.
resolved_concerns: Author addressed stickies-v's ownership/lifetime concern conceptually (non-owning handle pattern already used elsewhere in kernel code), and stickies-v said 'I agree then that there is no need for context to own the logging connection,' though the concrete use_count safeguard is not yet coded.

categories.name: kernel
categories.evidence: The PR changes bitcoinkernel.h/.cpp/_wrapper.h logging API surface directly: signatures of btck_logging_set_options/set_level_category/enable_category/disable_category, removal of btck_logging_disable, and a new btck_context_options_set_logger tying Logger to Context. This is squarely the kernel C API boundary.
categories.rationale: Author states the current API is 'too complicated and too restrictive,' with an unsafe btck_logging_disable() that 'will abort the program' if misused, and a wasteful default 1MB message buffer; this PR removes both. Six other open kernel PRs (#30342, #34374, #34775, #35322, #36197, #36207) touch the same logging surface, showing this is a live, contested design area whose resolution has leverage over multiple follow-on PRs, but it is not a correctness or fund-safety issue and the API is still explicitly experimental, so P2 rather than P1.

result.card: This draft PR redesigns the libbitcoinkernel C logging API so that log options and streams attach explicitly to Logger and Context objects instead of being global, removing the unsafe btck_logging_disable() and the default 1MB message-buffering behavior. It solves a real design problem for kernel API consumers, especially language-binding authors, per the author's own detailed rationale, and is explicitly meant to pave the way for a larger follow-up (#30342) that would let different log streams receive different messages. Six other open kernel PRs touch overlapping logging surface, showing this is a contested, high-leverage design area, but reviewers stickies-v and stringintech want it deferred until #30342 lands rather than locking in intermediate API shape, and stickies-v raised an unresolved Context/logger lifetime concern that the author addressed only conceptually. The PR needs a rebase and the author has been silent for roughly 200+ days since the last push, so it is Stale for review purposes even though the underlying problem remains real and unresolved.
